question: In its answers to questions for written answer E-004470/20251 and E-000611/20262, the Commission did not provide a clear answer to the question of whether the absence of a judicial remedy against a wrongful failure to refer is compatible with Article 19(1) of the Treaty on European Union (TEU) and Article 47 of the Charter of Fundamental Rights of the European Union (CFR).

According to the CILFIT judgment (Case C-283/81), a court of final instance is exempt from the obligation to refer a question for a preliminary ruling under Article 267(3) of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU) only in exceptional circumstances. According to the Remling judgment (Case C-767/23), the court must provide specific and concrete reasons for the non-referral. 1.

Does the Commission consider the absence of a legal remedy before a specialised court in the event of a breach of these obligations to be compatible with Article 19(1) TEU and Article 47 CFR, and if so, on what basis under EU law?
If not, what specific requirements does this entail for the Member States?

If the Commission does not systematically record infringements of the obligations to refer and to state reasons for non-referral set out in the CILFIT and Remling judgments, how can it possibly identify any structural deficits or systematic breaches as referred to in its previous replies?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (27.7.2026) As provided for in the second subparagraph of Article 19(1) Treaty on European Union, it is for the Member States to establish a system of legal remedies and procedures ensuring compliance with the right to effective judicial protection in the fields covered by EU law.

The principle of effective judicial protection is a general principle of EU law stemming from the constitutional traditions common to the Member States, which has been enshrined in Articles 6 and 13 of the Convention for the Protection of Human Rights and Fundamental Freedoms, and is reaffirmed in Article 47 of the Charter of Fundamental Rights of the European Union1.

As the Commission explained in its answers to written questions E-000611/2026 and E004470/2025, Article 267 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU) sets up a dialogue between the Court of Justice of the European Union and the courts of the Member States, in which the latter are closely involved in the uniform interpretation and correct application of EU law and the protection of individual rights.

It should be reiterated that the Commission monitors structural deficits in the dialogue under Article 267 TFEU. As guardian of the Treaties, the Commission may initiate infringement proceedings under Article 258 TFEU for possible non-compliance with Article 267(3) TFEU when a Member State adopts legislation preventing proper judicial cooperation under that provision, or when evidence points to a systematic breach.
1 Judgment of 11 May 2023, Inspecţia Judiciară, C-817/21, EU:C:2023:391, para. 40; judgment of 21 December
2021, Euro Box Promotion and Others, C‑357/19, C‑379/19, C‑547/19, C‑811/19 and C‑840/19, EU:C:2021:1034, para. 219 and the case-law cited.
